title: Maulvi Tamizuddin Khan v. Federation of Pakistan
parties: Maulvi Tamizuddin Khan v. Federation of Pakistan
description: Cited by the Supreme Court of Pakistan as the case in which the doctrine of necessity was first contrived.
fullText: At the inception of the creation of Pakistan as an independent State, this Court contrived the doctrine of necessity in the Maulvi Tamizuddin case 15 which was an invitation to future adventurers to suppress the will of the people. 15 (PLD 1955 FC 240)

title: State v. Dosso
description: Cited by the Supreme Court of Pakistan as the judgment that laid the foundation for legitimising martial law.
fullText: The foundation for legitimising a martial law was laid down by this Court in the Dosso case 16. 16 (PLD 1958 SC 533). The revered Dorab Patel describes the judgment in these words, 'Justice Cornelius's judgment in Dosso's case was a disaster for millions of people living in the former provinces of Baluchistan and the Frontier Province.

title: Asma Jilani v. Government of Punjab
parties: Asma Jilani v. Government of Punjab
description: Cited by the Supreme Court of Pakistan for the principle that an illegitimate usurper's legal order is not a valid source of law and cannot be recognised as de jure.
fullText: The Provisional Constitutional Orders issued during the martial law imposed by General Agha Mohammad Yahya Khan between 1968 to 1971 were subsequently declared to be of no legal validity by this Court in the Asma Jilani case 19. 19 (PLD 1972 SC 139). It was further observed that when a person destroys the national legal order in an illegitimate manner then the latter cannot be regarded as a valid source of law making.

title: Begum Nusrat Bhutto v. Chief of Army Staff
parties: Begum Nusrat Bhutto v. Chief of Army Staff
description: Cited by the Supreme Court of Pakistan in discussing the validation of the 1977 martial law and the power to amend the Constitution.
fullText: On July 05, 1977, less than five years from handing down of the judgment in the Asma Jilani case another usurper, General Zia ul Haq abrogated the Constitution. The judges of the Supreme Court preferred to become collaborators of the usurper by purportedly legitimising the high treason and declaring it as a 'revolution' and a 'new order' through the judgment in the Begum Nusrat Bhutto case. 21 (PLD 1977 SC 657). He was also given the power to amend the Constitution.

title: Muhammad Amir Khan v. Controller of Estate Duty
parties: Muhammad Amir Khan v. Controller of Estate Duty
description: Cited in the Supreme Court's review-jurisdiction judgment concerning the scope of Article 188 of the 1973 Constitution.
fullText: The 2023 Act is attached as an Annex to this judgment. In Constitutional Petition No.22/2023, Mr. Zaman Khan Vardag, ASC has contended that review jurisdiction under Article 188 of the 1973 Constitution is substantially and materially different than the appellate jurisdiction of this Court exercised under Article 185. He further relies upon the judgements of this Court reported as Muhammad Amir Khan v. Controller of Estate Duty (PLD 1962 SC 335) and Rashid Ahmed v. Irshad Ahmed (1968 SCMR 12).

title: Manzoor Elahi v. Federation of Pakistan
parties: Manzoor Elahi v. Federation of Pakistan
description: Cited by the Supreme Court of Pakistan for elaborating the meaning and scope of Article 184(3) of the Constitution.
fullText: After the coming into force of the Constitution in 1973, it did not take much time that the question as to the nature and scope of the original jurisdiction conferred on this Court under Article 184(3), came for consideration before this Court in Manzoor Elahi. The Court not only elaborated the meaning and scope of the phrase 'question of public importance with reference to the enforcement of any of the Fundamental Rights' as used in Article 184(3) but also explained the different contours of this jurisdiction. Manzoor Elahi v. Federation of Pakistan PLD 1975 SC 66.

title: Supreme Court Bar Association of Pakistan v. Federation of Pakistan
parties: Supreme Court Bar Association of Pakistan v. Federation of Pakistan

title: Shuhada Forum v. Justice (R) Jawwad S. Khawaja
citation: I.C.A. No. 5 of 2023 in C.P. No. 24 of 2023
parties: Shuhada Forum, Balochistan v. Justice (R) Jawwad S. Khawaja and others

fullText: I.C.A. 5/2023 in C.P. 24/2023 and C.M.A.10534/2023, Shuhada Forum, Balochistan through its Patron in Chief, Nawabzada Jamal Raisani, Quetta Cantt and others v. Justice (R) Jawwad S.
